questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As a highly ambitious student with a strong interest in small animal emergency and intensive care, I wanted an exchange destination that would provide advanced clinical experience in a high-standard teaching hospital. The University of Sydney was ideal because of its well-structured clinical rotations, access to specialized services, and exposure to unique aspects of veterinary medicine, such as Australian wildlife. Additionally, its reputation for hands-on learning and student involvement in patient care made it a perfect fit for my career goals.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not easy. Information was scattered across different platforms, and I had to reach out to various contacts to get clarity on administrative procedures, schedules, and logistics. A more centralized and comprehensive guide for incoming exchange students would have been helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received great assistance from the staff at Camden campus, especially from Debbie Sheehan, who was incredibly helpful in guiding me through the process. However, I received less assistance from staff at Camperdown campus, and I had to figure out many things on my own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding off-campus housing was fairly easy. I found a room in a shared house right across the street from campus through a Facebook group for USYD students. The trickiest part was having interviews with future roommates over video calls, but overall, the process went smoothly. I highly recommend joining Facebook housing groups and starting the search early to secure a convenient location.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Location is everything! Sydney is much bigger than it looks on a map, and public transportation can take hours depending on where you live. This is not ideal when you're expected to spend 8–10 hours at the hospital daily, often starting early and finishing late. I strongly recommend finding a place as close to campus as possible to save time, energy, and unnecessary commuting stress.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No student housing was available through USYD.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everything was ready for me upon arrival, so no additional registration at the university was needed. I received my name badge at the student support office at the Camperdown campus and my access card during orientation day at the small animal hospital.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student support office had staff available to assist with administrative questions, and I could also get help over email with fast response times.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The process went very smoothly, and I got into the courses I wanted. However, I did not get them in my preferred order. Instead, I was placed in a single study group for the duration of my rotations rather than changing groups every two weeks. This turned out to be beneficial, as it allowed me to build stronger connections with my group and settle into a routine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to inform the university of your arrival date well in advance so they can prepare your name badge and access card ahead of time. This will help streamline your first few days on campus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were at the master’s level and consisted of clinical rotations at the university teaching hospital under the guidance of senior veterinarians. The training was intensive and hands-on, providing valuable experience in real patient cases.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was more interactive, and students were given more responsibility, which significantly boosted our confidence. We were trusted to make clinical decisions under supervision and had a more active role in patient care. Additionally, spending two weeks on each service (instead of shorter rotations) gave us enough time to become comfortable with the workflow and fully absorb what we were learning.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Wildlife Medicine
- Surgery
- Anaesthesia
- Referral Medicine
- Emergency and Critical Care
- Primary Care

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I highly recommend:

Wildlife Medicine – This is a unique opportunity to work with Australian wildlife, something we don’t get much exposure to in Denmark. It is incredibly rewarding and a rare experience for European veterinary students.
Referral Medicine – The senior veterinarians in this rotation are outstanding teachers, and the cases are complex and challenging, requiring critical thinking and research.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately, there were no organized cultural, athletic, or social activities specifically for exchange students in veterinary medicine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend traveling along the east coast of Australia before or after the exchange. I personally visited Noosa and Fraser Island and had an amazing experience. Since Australia is so far away, it’s worth taking the time to explore the country while you're there.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! My Australian classmates were incredibly warm and welcoming, making the transition smooth.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The students have been studying together for over six years, so their friend groups are well-established. However, they are very friendly and welcoming if you take the initiative. Be outgoing—don’t hesitate to ask if you can join them for lunch, drinks, or dinner after school. They will always say yes!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I noticed a significant difference in the approach to treating animals with severe diseases. In Australia, there is a stronger inclination to pursue advanced diagnostics and treatments, even in cases where euthanasia might be a more common decision in Denmark. This was interesting to observe and made me reflect on different perspectives in veterinary medicine.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the active lifestyle in Australia. People make the most of nature, spending time at the beach, in the forest, or doing outdoor activities whenever they get the chance. The culture of waking up early and starting the day with exercise or time outdoors was something I really enjoyed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Start planning early! I started planning my exchange almost two years in advance, and it really helped me secure funding, housing, and my preferred courses.
Find accommodation close to the university. The hours at the hospital are long, and Sydney is a massive city—commuting for hours every day can be exhausting. Living nearby will save you valuable time and energy.
Make time to enjoy Australia! The veterinary courses at USYD are demanding, both mentally and physically. It’s easy to get completely absorbed in school, but don’t forget to take breaks. Plan your weekends and explore—you’re in one of the most beautiful countries in the world!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that you need to buy all your own clinical scrubs. Each rotation has different clothing requirements, so instead of buying everything new, I recommend buying second-hand from older students. There’s a Facebook group where students sell their used scrubs, which is a great way to save money and avoid unnecessary purchases.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The most rewarding aspects were:

The friendships I made—I met incredible people and built lifelong friendships.
Expanding my professional network—I had the opportunity to work with highly skilled senior veterinarians and gained valuable contacts for my future career.
The immense learning experience—both theoretically and practically, I have grown so much as a future veterinarian.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The biggest challenge was the long and exhausting hours at the hospital. Some days were 10–12 hours long, with a constant high patient flow and no real breaks. It was an adjustment to work at that intensity, but in the end, it helped me develop resilience and time management skills.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
